Spectrum.plot.description:
Separate plots are drawn for each channel type. When the data have been
processed with a bandpass, lowpass or highpass filter, dashed lines (╎)
indicate the boundaries of the filter. The line noise frequency is also
indicated with a dashed line (⋮). If ``average=False``, the plot will
be interactive, and click-dragging on the spectrum will generate a
scalp topography plot for the chosen frequency range in a new figure.

dB.description:
Whether to plot on a decibel scale. If ``True``, plots
10 × log₁₀(spectral_power/Hz).

color.description:
A matplotlib-compatible color to use for the curves. Defaults to
white.

fig_facecolor.description: A matplotlib-compatible color to use for the figure background. Defaults to black.

axis_facecolor.description:
A matplotlib-compatible color to use for the axis background.
Defaults to black.

block.description:
Whether to halt program execution until the figure is closed.
May not work on all systems / platforms. Defaults to ``False``.

Spectrum.plot_topo.description: Plot power spectral density, separately for each channel.

bands.description:
The frequencies or frequency ranges to plot. If a :class:`dict`, keys will
be used as subplot titles and values should be either a single frequency
(e.g., ``{'presentation rate': 6.5}``) or a length-two sequence of lower
and upper frequency band edges (e.g., ``{'theta': (4, 8)}``). If a single
frequency is provided, the plot will show the frequency bin that is closest
to the requested value. If ``None`` (the default), expands to::

    bands = {'Delta (0-4 Hz)': (0, 4), 'Theta (4-8 Hz)': (4, 8),
             'Alpha (8-12 Hz)': (8, 12), 'Beta (12-30 Hz)': (12, 30),
             'Gamma (30-45 Hz)': (30, 45)}

.. note::
   For backwards compatibility, :class:`tuples<tuple>` of length 2 or 3 are
   also accepted, where the last element of the tuple is the subplot title
   and the other entries are frequency values (a single value or band
   edges). New code should use :class:`dict` or ``None``.

.. versionchanged:: 1.2
   Allow passing a dict and discourage passing tuples.

ch_type.description:
The channel type to plot. For ``'grad'``, the gradiometers are
collected in pairs and the mean for each pair is plotted. If
``None`` the first available channel type from order shown above is used. Defaults to ``None``.

normalize.description:
If True, each band will be divided by the total power. Defaults to
False.

agg_fun.description:
The function used to aggregate over frequencies. Defaults to
:func:`numpy.sum` if ``normalize=True``, else :func:`numpy.mean`.

dB.description:
Whether to plot on a decibel scale. If ``True``, plots
10 × log₁₀(spectral_power/Hz), following the application of ``agg_fun``. Ignored if ``normalize=True``.

sensors.description:
Whether to add markers for sensor locations. If :class:`str`, should be a
valid matplotlib format string (e.g., ``'r+'`` for red plusses, see the
Notes section of :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.plot`). If ``True`` (the
default), black circles will be used.

show_names.description:
If ``True``, show channel names next to each sensor marker. If callable,
channel names will be formatted using the callable; e.g., to
delete the prefix 'MEG ' from all channel names, pass the function
``lambda x: x.replace('MEG ', '')``. If ``mask`` is not ``None``, only
non-masked sensor names will be shown.

mask.description:
Array indicating channel-time combinations to highlight with a distinct
plotting style (useful for, e.g. marking which channels at which times a statistical test of the data reaches significance). Array elements set to ``True`` will be plotted
with the parameters given in ``mask_params``. Defaults to ``None``,
equivalent to an array of all ``False`` elements.

mask_params.description:
Additional plotting parameters for plotting significant sensors.
Default (None) equals::

    dict(marker='o', markerfacecolor='w', markeredgecolor='k',
            linewidth=0, markersize=4)

contours.description:
The number of contour lines to draw. If ``0``, no contours will be drawn.
If a positive integer, that number of contour levels are chosen using the
matplotlib tick locator (may sometimes be inaccurate, use array for
accuracy). If array-like, the array values are used as the contour levels.
The values should be in µV for EEG, fT for magnetometers and fT/m for
gradiometers. If ``colorbar=True``, the colorbar will have ticks
corresponding to the contour levels. Default is ``6``.

outlines.description:
The outlines to be drawn. If 'head', the default head scheme will be
drawn. If dict, each key refers to a tuple of x and y positions, the values
in 'mask_pos' will serve as image mask.
Alternatively, a matplotlib patch object can be passed for advanced
masking options, either directly or as a function that returns patches
(required for multi-axis plots). If None, nothing will be drawn.
Defaults to 'head'.

image_interp.description:
The image interpolation to be used. Options are ``'cubic'`` (default)
to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.CloughTocher2DInterpolator`,
``'nearest'`` to use :class:`scipy.spatial.Voronoi` or
``'linear'`` to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.LinearNDInterpolator`.

extrapolate.description:
Options:

- ``'box'``
    Extrapolate to four points placed to form a square encompassing all
    data points, where each side of the square is three times the range
    of the data in the respective dimension.
- ``'local'`` (default for MEG sensors)
    Extrapolate only to nearby points (approximately to points closer than
    median inter-electrode distance). This will also set the
    mask to be polygonal based on the convex hull of the sensors.
- ``'head'`` (default for non-MEG sensors)
    Extrapolate out to the edges of the clipping circle. This will be on
    the head circle when the sensors are contained within the head circle,
    but it can extend beyond the head when sensors are plotted outside
    the head circle.

border.description:
Value to extrapolate to on the topomap borders. If ``'mean'`` (default),
then each extrapolated point has the average value of its neighbours.

res.description: The resolution of the topomap image (number of pixels along each side).

size.description: Side length of each subplot in inches.

vlim.description:
Lower and upper bounds of the colormap, typically a numeric value in the same
units as the data. Elements of the :class:`tuple` may also be callable functions
which take in a :class:`NumPy array <numpy.ndarray>` and return a scalar.

If both entries are ``None``, the bounds are set at ± the maximum absolute value
of the data (yielding a colormap with midpoint at 0), or ``(0, max(abs(data)))``
if the (possibly baselined) data are all-positive.
Providing ``None`` for just one entry will set the corresponding boundary at the
min/max of the data. If ``vlim="joint"``, will compute the colormap limits
jointly across all topomaps of the same channel type (instead of separately
for each topomap), using the min/max of the data for that channel type.
Defaults to ``(None, None)``.

colorbar.description: Plot a colorbar in the rightmost column of the figure.

cbar_fmt.description:
Formatting string for colorbar tick labels. See :ref:`formatspec` for
details.
If ``'auto'``, is equivalent to '%0.3f' if ``dB=False`` and '%0.1f' if
``dB=True``. Defaults to ``'auto'``.

units.description:
The units to use for the colorbar label. Ignored if ``colorbar=False``.
If ``None`` the label will be "AU" indicating arbitrary units.
Default is ``None``.

add_list.description:

The channels contained in the other instances are appended to the
channels of the current instance. Therefore, all other instances
must be of the same type as the current object.

ref_channels.description:

recording. This is useful when you need to re-reference your data
to different channels. These added channels will consist of all zeros.

Notes section of :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.plot`). If ``True`` (the
default), black circles will be used.

show_names.description:
If ``True``, show channel names next to each sensor marker. If callable,
channel names will be formatted using the callable; e.g., to
delete the prefix 'MEG ' from all channel names, pass the function
``lambda x: x.replace('MEG ', '')``. If ``mask`` is not ``None``, only
non-masked sensor names will be shown.

mask.description:
Array indicating channel-time combinations to highlight with a distinct
plotting style (useful for, e.g. marking which channels at which times a statistical test of the data reaches significance). Array elements set to ``True`` will be plotted
with the parameters given in ``mask_params``. Defaults to ``None``,
equivalent to an array of all ``False`` elements.

mask_params.description:
Additional plotting parameters for plotting significant sensors.
Default (None) equals::

    dict(marker='o', markerfacecolor='w', markeredgecolor='k',
            linewidth=0, markersize=4)

contours.description:
The number of contour lines to draw. If ``0``, no contours will be drawn.
If a positive integer, that number of contour levels are chosen using the
matplotlib tick locator (may sometimes be inaccurate, use array for
accuracy). If array-like, the array values are used as the contour levels.
The values should be in µV for EEG, fT for magnetometers and fT/m for
gradiometers. If ``colorbar=True``, the colorbar will have ticks
corresponding to the contour levels. Default is ``6``.

outlines.description:
The outlines to be drawn. If 'head', the default head scheme will be
drawn. If dict, each key refers to a tuple of x and y positions, the values
in 'mask_pos' will serve as image mask.
Alternatively, a matplotlib patch object can be passed for advanced
masking options, either directly or as a function that returns patches
(required for multi-axis plots). If None, nothing will be drawn.
Defaults to 'head'.

image_interp.description:
The image interpolation to be used. Options are ``'cubic'`` (default)
to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.CloughTocher2DInterpolator`,
``'nearest'`` to use :class:`scipy.spatial.Voronoi` or
``'linear'`` to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.LinearNDInterpolator`.

extrapolate.description:
Options:

- ``'box'``
    Extrapolate to four points placed to form a square encompassing all
    data points, where each side of the square is three times the range
    of the data in the respective dimension.
- ``'local'`` (default for MEG sensors)
    Extrapolate only to nearby points (approximately to points closer than
    median inter-electrode distance). This will also set the
    mask to be polygonal based on the convex hull of the sensors.
- ``'head'`` (default for non-MEG sensors)
    Extrapolate out to the edges of the clipping circle. This will be on
    the head circle when the sensors are contained within the head circle,
    but it can extend beyond the head when sensors are plotted outside
    the head circle.

border.description:
Value to extrapolate to on the topomap borders. If ``'mean'`` (default),
then each extrapolated point has the average value of its neighbours.

res.description: The resolution of the topomap image (number of pixels along each side).

size.description: Side length of each subplot in inches.

vlim.description:
Lower and upper bounds of the colormap, typically a numeric value in the same
units as the data. Elements of the :class:`tuple` may also be callable functions
which take in a :class:`NumPy array <numpy.ndarray>` and return a scalar.

of the data (yielding a colormap with midpoint at 0), or ``(0, max(abs(data)))``
if the (possibly baselined) data are all-positive.

min/max of the data. If ``vlim="joint"``, will compute the colormap limits
jointly across all topomaps of the same channel type (instead of separately
for each topomap), using the min/max of the data for that channel type.
Defaults to ``(None, None)``.

details.
If ``'auto'``, is equivalent to '%0.3f' if ``dB=False`` and '%0.1f' if
``dB=True``. Defaults to ``'auto'``.

units.description:
The units to use for the colorbar label. Ignored if ``colorbar=False``.

picks.description:

'eeg']``) will pick channels of those types, channel *name* strings (e.g.,

:term:`data channels`. None (default) will pick all channels. Bad channels 
are included by default. Note that channels in ``info['bads']`` *will be 
included* if their names or indices are explicitly provided.

integer index (:class:`pandas.RangeIndex`) will be used. If a

will be used. Defaults to ``None``.

long_format.description:

observation of the signal at a unique combination of frequency and channel.

verbose.description:

verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

    In version 1.8, the default changed to ``amplitude=False``.

Default is ``sd``.

    ``exclude=()``.

indicate the boundaries of the filter. The line noise frequency is also
indicated with a dashed line (⋮). If ``average=False``, the plot will
be interactive, and click-dragging on the spectrum will generate a
scalp topography plot for the chosen frequency range in a new figure.

average.description:
Whether to average across channels before plotting. If ``True``, interactive
plotting of scalp topography is disabled, and parameters ``ci`` and
``ci_alpha`` control the style of the confidence band around the mean.
Default is ``False``.

dB.description:
Whether to plot on a decibel scale. If ``True``, plots
10 × log₁₀(spectral_power/Hz), or 20 × log₁₀(spectral amplitude/√Hz) if ``amplitude=True``.

amplitude.description:
Whether to plot an amplitude spectrum (``True``) or power spectrum
(``False``).

.. versionchanged:: 1.8
    In version 1.8, the default changed to ``amplitude=False``.

xscale.description: Scale of the frequency axis. Default is ``'linear'``.

ci.description:
Type of confidence band drawn around the mean when ``average=True``. If
``'sd'`` the band spans ±1 standard deviation across channels. If
``'range'`` the band spans the range across channels at each frequency. If a
:class:`float`, it indicates the (bootstrapped) confidence interval to
display, and must satisfy ``0 < ci <= 100``. If ``None``, no band is drawn.
Default is ``sd``.

ci_alpha.description:
Opacity of the confidence band. Must satisfy ``0 <= ci_alpha <= 1``. Default
is 0.3.

color.description:
A matplotlib-compatible color to use. Has no effect when
spatial_colors=True.

alpha.description:
Opacity of the spectrum line(s). If :class:`float`, must satisfy
``0 <= alpha <= 1``. If ``None``, opacity will be ``1`` when
``average=True`` and ``0.1`` when ``average=False``. Default is ``None``.

spatial_colors.description:
Whether to color spectrum lines by channel location. Ignored if
``average=True``.

exclude.description:
Channel names to exclude from being drawn. If ``'bads'``, channels
in ``spectrum.info['bads']`` are excluded; pass an empty list to
include all channels (including "bad" channels, if any).

.. versionchanged:: 1.5
    In version 1.5, the default behavior changed from ``exclude='bads'`` to
    ``exclude=()``.

EpochsSpectrumArray.plot.description:
Separate plots are drawn for each channel type. When the data have been
processed with a bandpass, lowpass or highpass filter, dashed lines (╎)
indicate the boundaries of the filter. The line noise frequency is also
indicated with a dashed line (⋮). If ``average=False``, the plot will
be interactive, and click-dragging on the spectrum will generate a
scalp topography plot for the chosen frequency range in a new figure.

dB.description:
Whether to plot on a decibel scale. If ``True``, plots
10 × log₁₀(spectral_power/Hz).

color.description:
A matplotlib-compatible color to use for the curves. Defaults to
white.

fig_facecolor.description: A matplotlib-compatible color to use for the figure background. Defaults to black.

axis_facecolor.description:
A matplotlib-compatible color to use for the axis background.
Defaults to black.

block.description:
Whether to halt program execution until the figure is closed.
May not work on all systems / platforms. Defaults to ``False``.

EpochsSpectrumArray.plot_topo.description: Plot power spectral density, separately for each channel.

bands.description:
The frequencies or frequency ranges to plot. If a :class:`dict`, keys will
be used as subplot titles and values should be either a single frequency
(e.g., ``{'presentation rate': 6.5}``) or a length-two sequence of lower
and upper frequency band edges (e.g., ``{'theta': (4, 8)}``). If a single
frequency is provided, the plot will show the frequency bin that is closest
to the requested value. If ``None`` (the default), expands to::

    bands = {'Delta (0-4 Hz)': (0, 4), 'Theta (4-8 Hz)': (4, 8),
             'Alpha (8-12 Hz)': (8, 12), 'Beta (12-30 Hz)': (12, 30),
             'Gamma (30-45 Hz)': (30, 45)}

.. note::
   For backwards compatibility, :class:`tuples<tuple>` of length 2 or 3 are
   also accepted, where the last element of the tuple is the subplot title
   and the other entries are frequency values (a single value or band
   edges). New code should use :class:`dict` or ``None``.

.. versionchanged:: 1.2
   Allow passing a dict and discourage passing tuples.

ch_type.description:
The channel type to plot. For ``'grad'``, the gradiometers are
collected in pairs and the mean for each pair is plotted. If
``None`` the first available channel type from order shown above is used. Defaults to ``None``.

normalize.description:
If True, each band will be divided by the total power. Defaults to
False.

agg_fun.description:
The function used to aggregate over frequencies. Defaults to
:func:`numpy.sum` if ``normalize=True``, else :func:`numpy.mean`.

dB.description:
Whether to plot on a decibel scale. If ``True``, plots
10 × log₁₀(spectral_power/Hz), following the application of ``agg_fun``. Ignored if ``normalize=True``.

sensors.description:
Whether to add markers for sensor locations. If :class:`str`, should be a
valid matplotlib format string (e.g., ``'r+'`` for red plusses, see the
Notes section of :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.plot`). If ``True`` (the
default), black circles will be used.

show_names.description:
If ``True``, show channel names next to each sensor marker. If callable,
channel names will be formatted using the callable; e.g., to
delete the prefix 'MEG ' from all channel names, pass the function
``lambda x: x.replace('MEG ', '')``. If ``mask`` is not ``None``, only
non-masked sensor names will be shown.

mask.description:
Array indicating channel-time combinations to highlight with a distinct
plotting style (useful for, e.g. marking which channels at which times a statistical test of the data reaches significance). Array elements set to ``True`` will be plotted
with the parameters given in ``mask_params``. Defaults to ``None``,
equivalent to an array of all ``False`` elements.

mask_params.description:
Additional plotting parameters for plotting significant sensors.
Default (None) equals::

    dict(marker='o', markerfacecolor='w', markeredgecolor='k',
            linewidth=0, markersize=4)

contours.description:
The number of contour lines to draw. If ``0``, no contours will be drawn.
If a positive integer, that number of contour levels are chosen using the
matplotlib tick locator (may sometimes be inaccurate, use array for
accuracy). If array-like, the array values are used as the contour levels.
The values should be in µV for EEG, fT for magnetometers and fT/m for
gradiometers. If ``colorbar=True``, the colorbar will have ticks
corresponding to the contour levels. Default is ``6``.

outlines.description:
The outlines to be drawn. If 'head', the default head scheme will be
drawn. If dict, each key refers to a tuple of x and y positions, the values
in 'mask_pos' will serve as image mask.
Alternatively, a matplotlib patch object can be passed for advanced
masking options, either directly or as a function that returns patches
(required for multi-axis plots). If None, nothing will be drawn.
Defaults to 'head'.

image_interp.description:
The image interpolation to be used. Options are ``'cubic'`` (default)
to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.CloughTocher2DInterpolator`,
``'nearest'`` to use :class:`scipy.spatial.Voronoi` or
``'linear'`` to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.LinearNDInterpolator`.

extrapolate.description:
Options:

- ``'box'``
    Extrapolate to four points placed to form a square encompassing all
    data points, where each side of the square is three times the range
    of the data in the respective dimension.
- ``'local'`` (default for MEG sensors)
    Extrapolate only to nearby points (approximately to points closer than
    median inter-electrode distance). This will also set the
    mask to be polygonal based on the convex hull of the sensors.
- ``'head'`` (default for non-MEG sensors)
    Extrapolate out to the edges of the clipping circle. This will be on
    the head circle when the sensors are contained within the head circle,
    but it can extend beyond the head when sensors are plotted outside
    the head circle.

border.description:
Value to extrapolate to on the topomap borders. If ``'mean'`` (default),
then each extrapolated point has the average value of its neighbours.

res.description: The resolution of the topomap image (number of pixels along each side).

size.description: Side length of each subplot in inches.

vlim.description:
Lower and upper bounds of the colormap, typically a numeric value in the same
units as the data. Elements of the :class:`tuple` may also be callable functions
which take in a :class:`NumPy array <numpy.ndarray>` and return a scalar.

If both entries are ``None``, the bounds are set at ± the maximum absolute value
of the data (yielding a colormap with midpoint at 0), or ``(0, max(abs(data)))``
if the (possibly baselined) data are all-positive.
Providing ``None`` for just one entry will set the corresponding boundary at the
min/max of the data. If ``vlim="joint"``, will compute the colormap limits
jointly across all topomaps of the same channel type (instead of separately
for each topomap), using the min/max of the data for that channel type.
Defaults to ``(None, None)``.

colorbar.description: Plot a colorbar in the rightmost column of the figure.

cbar_fmt.description:
Formatting string for colorbar tick labels. See :ref:`formatspec` for
details.
If ``'auto'``, is equivalent to '%0.3f' if ``dB=False`` and '%0.1f' if
``dB=True``. Defaults to ``'auto'``.

units.description:
The units to use for the colorbar label. Ignored if ``colorbar=False``.
If ``None`` the label will be "AU" indicating arbitrary units.
Default is ``None``.

The computed filter is fitted to data from all of the picked channels,
with frequency response given by the standard IIR formula:

.. math::

    H(e^{jw}) = \frac{1}{a[0] + a[1]e^{-jw} + ... + a[n]e^{-jnw}}

and about time and frequency smoothing.

  slice along the time axis).

    Decimation is done after convolutions and may create aliasing
    artifacts.

a periodic window (``False``, for spectral analysis). Default is
``True``.

cycles.

(array-like).

sigma.description:
It controls the width of the wavelet ie its temporal
resolution. If sigma is None the temporal resolution
is adapted with the frequency like for all wavelet transform.
The higher the frequency the shorter is the wavelet.
If sigma is fixed the temporal resolution is fixed
like for the short time Fourier transform and the number
of oscillations increases with the frequency.

morlet.description: Compute Morlet wavelets for the given frequency range.

a divider of wsize and smaller than wsize/2) (default: wsize/2).

perfectly inverted. It only returns the positive frequencies.

tstep.description:

Number of cycles in the wavelet, either a fixed number or one per
frequency. The number of cycles ``n_cycles`` and the frequencies of
interest ``freqs`` define the temporal window length. See notes for
additional information about the relationship between those arguments
and about time and frequency smoothing.

zero_mean.description:
If True, make sure the wavelets have a mean of zero. default False.

.. versionchanged:: 1.8
    The default will change from ``zero_mean=False`` in 1.6 to ``True`` in
    1.8.

use_fft.description: Use the FFT for convolutions or not. default True.

decim.description:
Decimation factor, applied *after* time-frequency decomposition.

- if :class:`int`, returns ``tfr[..., ::decim]`` (keep only every Nth
  sample along the time axis).
- if :class:`slice`, returns ``tfr[..., decim]`` (keep only the specified
  slice along the time axis).

.. note::
    Decimation is done after convolutions and may create aliasing
    artifacts.

* ``'power'`` : single trial power.

* ``'avg_power_itc'`` : average of single trial power and inter-trial

as ``n_jobs=1`` (sequential execution) unless the call is performed under
a :class:`joblib:joblib.parallel_config` context manager that sets another
value for ``n_jobs``.
The number of epochs to process at the same time. The parallelization
is implemented across channels. Default 1.

resolution, if > 1, increased frequency resolution. Defaults to 1.

X.description: The signals.

use_fft.description: Use FFT for convolutions. Defaults to True.

mode.description:
Convention for convolution. 'full' is currently not implemented with
``use_fft=False``. Defaults to ``'same'``.

decim.description:
Decimation factor, applied *after* time-frequency decomposition.

- if :class:`int`, returns ``tfr[..., ::decim]`` (keep only every Nth
  sample along the time axis).

cwt.description: Compute time-frequency decomposition with continuous wavelet transform.

subject.description:
Subject name in Freesurfer subjects dir.

.. versionchanged:: 1.2
   This parameter was renamed from ``subject_id`` to ``subject``.

hemi.description:
Hemisphere id (ie 'lh', 'rh', 'both', or 'split'). In the case
of 'both', both hemispheres are shown in the same window.
In the case of 'split' hemispheres are displayed side-by-side
in different viewing panes.

title.description: Title for the window.

cortex.description:
Specifies how the cortical surface is rendered. Options:

1. The name of one of the preset cortex styles:
    ``'classic'`` (default), ``'high_contrast'``,
    ``'low_contrast'``, or ``'bone'``.
2. A single color-like argument to render the cortex as a single
    color, e.g. ``'red'`` or ``(0.1, 0.4, 1.)``.
3. A list of two color-like used to render binarized curvature
    values for gyral (first) and sulcal (second). regions, e.g.,
    ``['red', 'blue']`` or ``[(1, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1)]``.
4. A dict containing keys ``'vmin', 'vmax', 'colormap'`` with
    values used to render the binarized curvature (where 0 is gyral,
    1 is sulcal).

.. versionchanged:: 0.24
   Add support for non-string arguments.

size.description:
The size of the window, in pixels. can be one number to specify
a square window, or a length-2 sequence to specify (width, height).

foreground.description:
Color of the foreground (will be used for colorbars and text).
None (default) will use black or white depending on the value
of ``background``.

subjects_dir.description:
If not None, this directory will be used as the subjects directory
instead of the value set using the SUBJECTS_DIR environment
variable.

views.description:
View to use. Using multiple views (list) is not supported for mpl
backend. See :meth:`Brain.show_view <mne.viz.Brain.show_view>` for
valid string options.

offset.description:
If True, shifts the right- or left-most x coordinate of the left and
right surfaces, respectively, to be at zero. This is useful for viewing
inflated surface where hemispheres typically overlap. Can be "auto"
(default) use True with inflated surfaces and False otherwise
(Default: 'auto'). Only used when ``hemi='both'``.

.. versionchanged:: 0.23
   Default changed to "auto".

interaction.description:
Can be "trackball" (default) or "terrain", i.e. a turntable-style
camera.

units.description: Can be 'm' or 'mm' (default).

view_layout.description:
Can be "vertical" (default) or "horizontal". When using "horizontal" mode,
the PyVista backend must be used and hemi cannot be "split".

silhouette.description:
As a dict, it contains the ``color``, ``linewidth``, ``alpha`` opacity
and ``decimate`` (level of decimation between 0 and 1 or None) of the
brain's silhouette to display. If True, the default values are used
and if False, no silhouette will be displayed. Defaults to False.

theme.description:
Can be "auto", "light", or "dark" or a path-like to a
custom stylesheet. For Dark-Mode and automatic Dark-Mode-Detection,
`qdarkstyle <https://github.com/ColinDuquesnoy/QDarkStyleSheet>`__ and
`darkdetect <https://github.com/albertosottile/darkdetect>`__,
respectively, are required.    If None (default), the config option MNE_3D_OPTION_THEME will be used,
defaulting to "auto" if it's not found.

show.description: Display the window as soon as it is ready. Defaults to True.

Brain.description:
.. warning::
   The API for this class is not currently complete. We suggest using
   :meth:`mne.viz.plot_source_estimates` with the PyVista backend
   enabled to obtain a ``Brain`` instance.

time_viewer.description: If True, enable widgets interaction. Defaults to True.

show_traces.description: If True, enable visualization of time traces. Defaults to True.

value.description:
If True, the widgets are shown and if False, they
are hidden. If None, the state of the widgets is
toggled. Defaults to None.

If True, automatic time playback is enabled and if False,
it's disabled. If None, the state of time playback is toggled.
Defaults to None.

Brain.reset.description: Reset view, current time and time step.

hemi.description: The hemisphere id of the vertex.

vertex_id.description: The vertex identifier in the mesh.

color.description: The color of the time course.

update.description: Force an update of the plot. Defaults to True.
Force an update of the plot. Defaults to True.

Brain.plot_time_line.description: Add the time line to the MPL widget.

array.description:
Data array. For the data to be understood as vector-valued
(3 values per vertex corresponding to X/Y/Z surface RAS),
then ``array`` must be have all 3 dimensions.
If vectors with no time dimension are desired, consider using a
singleton (e.g., ``np.newaxis``) to create a "time" dimension
and pass ``time_label=None`` (vector values are not supported).

fmin.description: Minimum value in colormap (uses real fmin if None).

fmid.description:
Intermediate value in colormap (fmid between fmin and
fmax if None).

fmax.description: Maximum value in colormap (uses real max if None).

thresh.description:
Not supported yet.
If not None, values below thresh will not be visible.

center.description:
If not None, center of a divergent colormap, changes the meaning of
fmin, fmax and fmid.

transparent.description:
If True: use a linear transparency between fmin and fmid
and make values below fmin fully transparent (symmetrically for
divergent colormaps). None will choose automatically based on colormap
type.

colormap.description:
Name of matplotlib colormap to use, a list of matplotlib colors,
or a custom look up table (an n x 4 array coded with RBGA values
between 0 and 255), the default "auto" chooses a default divergent
colormap, if "center" is given (currently "icefire"), otherwise a
default sequential colormap (currently "rocket").

vertices.description:
Vertices for which the data is defined (needed if
``len(data) < nvtx``).

smoothing_steps.description:
Number of smoothing steps (smoothing is used if len(data) < nvtx)
The value 'nearest' can be used too. None (default) will use as
many as necessary to fill the surface.

time.description: Time points in the data array (if data is 2D or 3D).

time_label.description:
Format of the time label (a format string, a function that maps
floating point time values to strings, or None for no label). The
default is ``'auto'``, which will use ``time=%0.2f ms`` if there
is more than one time point.

colorbar.description:
Whether to add a colorbar to the figure. Can also be a tuple
to give the (row, col) index of where to put the colorbar.

hemi.description:
If None, it is assumed to belong to the hemisphere being
shown. If two hemispheres are being shown, an error will
be thrown.

remove_existing.description:
Not supported yet.
Remove surface added by previous "add_data" call. Useful for
conserving memory when displaying different data in a loop.

time_label_size.description: Font size of the time label (default 14).

initial_time.description:
Time initially shown in the plot. ``None`` to use the first time
sample (default).

scale_factor.description:
The scale factor to use when displaying glyphs for vector-valued
data.

vector_alpha.description:
Alpha level to control opacity of the arrows. Only used for
vector-valued data. If None (default), ``alpha`` is used.

volume_options.description:
Options for volumetric source estimate plotting, with key/value pairs:

- ``'resolution'`` : float | None
    Resolution (in mm) of volume rendering. Smaller (e.g., 1.) looks
    better at the cost of speed. None (default) uses the volume source
    space resolution, which is often something like 7 or 5 mm,
    without resampling.
- ``'blending'`` : str
    Can be "mip" (default) for :term:`maximum intensity projection` or
    "composite" for composite blending using alpha values.
- ``'alpha'`` : float | None
    Alpha for the volumetric rendering. Defaults are 0.4 for vector source
    estimates and 1.0 for scalar source estimates.
- ``'surface_alpha'`` : float | None
    Alpha for the surface enclosing the volume(s). None (default) will use
    half the volume alpha. Set to zero to avoid plotting the surface.
- ``'silhouette_alpha'`` : float | None
    Alpha for a silhouette along the outside of the volume. None (default)
    will use ``0.25 * surface_alpha``.
- ``'silhouette_linewidth'`` : float
    The line width to use for the silhouette. Default is 2.

A float input (default 1.) or None will be used for the ``'resolution'``
entry.

verbose.description:
Control verbosity of the logging output. If ``None``, use the default
verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

Brain.add_data.description:
This provides a similar interface to PySurfer, but it displays
it with a single colormap. It offers more flexibility over the
colormap, and provides a way to display four-dimensional data
(i.e., a timecourse) or five-dimensional data (i.e., a
vector-valued timecourse).

.. note:: ``fmin`` sets the low end of the colormap, and is separate
          from thresh (this is a different convention from PySurfer).

Brain.remove_data.description: Remove rendered data from the mesh.

Brain.remove_labels.description: Remove all the ROI labels from the image.

Brain.remove_annotations.description: Remove all annotations from the image.

scalar_thresh.description:
Threshold the label ids using this value in the label
file's scalar field (i.e. label only vertices with
scalar >= thresh).

borders.description:
Show only label borders. If int, specify the number of steps
(away from the true border) along the cortical mesh to include
as part of the border definition.

hemi.description:
If None, it is assumed to belong to the hemisphere being
shown.

subdir.description:
If a label is specified as name, subdir can be used to indicate
that the label file is in a sub-directory of the subject's
label directory rather than in the label directory itself (e.g.
for ``$SUBJECTS_DIR/$SUBJECT/label/aparc/lh.cuneus.label``
``brain.add_label('cuneus', subdir='aparc')``).

Brain.add_label.description: Add an ROI label to the image.

scale.description:
The size of the arrow representing the dipoles in
:class:`mne.viz.Brain` units. Default 1.5mm.

Brain.add_forward.description: Add a quiver to render positions of dipoles.

Brain.remove_forward.description: Remove forward sources from the rendered scene.

scales.description:
The size of the arrow representing the dipole in
:class:`mne.viz.Brain` units. Default 5mm.

mode.description:
The drawing mode for the dipole to render.
Defaults to ``"arrow"``.

Brain.add_dipole.description: Add a quiver to render positions of dipoles.

Brain.remove_dipole.description: Remove dipole objects from the rendered scene.

dense.description:
Whether to plot the dense head (``seghead``) or the less dense head
(``head``).

color.description: A list of anything matplotlib accepts: string, RGB, hex, etc.

Brain.add_head.description: Add a mesh to render the outer head surface.

Brain.remove_head.description: Remove head objects from the rendered scene.

outer.description: Adds the outer skull if ``True``, otherwise adds the inner skull.

color.description: A list of anything matplotlib accepts: string, RGB, hex, etc.

Brain.add_skull.description: Add a mesh to render the skull surface.

Brain.remove_skull.description: Remove skull objects from the rendered scene.

aseg.description:
The anatomical segmentation file. Default ``auto`` uses ``aparc+aseg``
if available and ``wmparc`` if not. This may be any anatomical
segmentation file in the mri subdirectory of the Freesurfer subject
directory.

.. versionchanged:: 1.8
   Added support for the new default ``'auto'``.

labels.description:
Labeled regions of interest to plot. See
:func:`mne.get_montage_volume_labels`
for one way to determine regions of interest. Regions can also be
chosen from the :term:`FreeSurfer LUT`.

fill_hole_size.description:
The size of holes to remove in the mesh in voxels. Default is None,
no holes are removed. Warning, this dilates the boundaries of the
surface by ``fill_hole_size`` number of voxels so use the minimal
size.

legend.description:
Add a legend displaying the names of the ``labels``. Default (None)
is ``True`` if the number of ``labels`` is 10 or fewer.
Can also be a dict of ``kwargs`` to pass to
``pyvista.Plotter.add_legend``.

Brain.add_volume_labels.description: Add labels to the rendering from an anatomical segmentation.

Brain.remove_volume_labels.description: Remove the volume labels from the rendered scene.

coords.description:
Coordinates in stereotaxic space (default) or array of
vertex ids (with ``coord_as_verts=True``).

coords_as_verts.description: Whether the coords parameter should be interpreted as vertex ids.

map_surface.description:
Surface to project the coordinates to, or None to use raw coords.
When set to a surface, each foci is positioned at the closest
vertex in the mesh.

scale_factor.description: Controls the size of the foci spheres (relative to 1cm).

color.description: A list of anything matplotlib accepts: string, RGB, hex, etc.

hemi.description:
If None, it is assumed to belong to the hemisphere being
shown. If two hemispheres are being shown, an error will
be thrown.

Brain.add_foci.description:
The foci spheres can be displayed at the coordinates given, or
mapped through a surface geometry. In other words, coordinates
from a volume-based analysis in MNI space can be displayed on an
inflated average surface by finding the closest vertex on the
white surface and mapping to that vertex on the inflated mesh.

meg.description:
Can be "helmet", "sensors" or "ref" to show the MEG helmet, sensors or
reference sensors respectively, or a combination like
``('helmet', 'sensors')`` (same as None, default). True translates to
``('helmet', 'sensors', 'ref')``. Can also be a dict to specify alpha values,
e.g. ``{"helmet": 0.1, "sensors": 0.8}``.

.. versionchanged:: 1.6
   Added support for specifying alpha values as a dict.

eeg.description:
String options are:

- "original" (default; equivalent to ``True``)
    Shows EEG sensors using their digitized locations (after
    transformation to the chosen ``coord_frame``)
- "projected"
    The EEG locations projected onto the scalp, as is done in
    forward modeling

Can also be a list of these options, or a dict to specify the alpha values
to use, e.g. ``dict(original=0.2, projected=0.8)``.

.. versionchanged:: 1.6
   Added support for specifying alpha values as a dict.

fnirs.description:
Can be "channels", "pairs", "detectors", and/or "sources" to show the
fNIRS channel locations, optode locations, or line between
source-detector pairs, or a combination like ``('pairs', 'channels')``.
True translates to ``('pairs',)``. A dict can also be used to specify
alpha values (but only "channels" and "pairs" will be used), e.g.
``dict(channels=0.2, pairs=0.7)``.

.. versionchanged:: 1.6
   Added support for specifying alpha values as a dict.

dbs.description: If True (default), show DBS (deep brain stimulation) electrodes.

max_dist.description:
The maximum distance to project a sensor to the pial surface in meters.
Sensors that are greater than this distance from the pial surface will
not be assigned locations. Projections can be done to the inflated or
flat brain.

sensor_colors.description:
Colors to use for the sensor glyphs. Can be None (default) to use default colors.
A dict should provide the colors (values) for each channel type (keys), e.g.::

    dict(eeg=eeg_colors)

Where the value (``eeg_colors`` above) can be broadcast to an array of colors with
length that matches the number of channels of that type, i.e., is compatible with
:func:`matplotlib.colors.to_rgba_array`. A few examples of this for the case above
are the string ``"k"``, a list of ``n_eeg`` color strings, or an NumPy ndarray of
shape ``(n_eeg, 3)`` or ``(n_eeg, 4)``.

.. versionadded:: 1.6

sensor_scales.description:
Scale to use for the sensor glyphs. Can be None (default) to use default scale.
A dict should provide the Scale (values) for each channel type (keys), e.g.::

    dict(eeg=eeg_scales)

Where the value (``eeg_scales`` above) can be broadcast to an array of values with
length that matches the number of channels of that type. A few examples of this
for the case above are the value ``10e-3``, a list of ``n_eeg`` values, or an NumPy
ndarray of shape ``(n_eeg,)``.

.. versionadded:: 1.9

verbose.description:
Control verbosity of the logging output. If ``None``, use the default
verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

Brain.add_sensors.description: Add mesh objects to represent sensor positions.

kind.description:
If None, removes all sensor-related data including the helmet.
Can be "meg", "eeg", "fnirs", "ecog", "seeg", "dbs" or "helmet"
to remove that item.

Brain.remove_sensors.description: Remove sensors from the rendered scene.

initialization (default is black or white depending on the
background color).

col.description:

column.

font_file.description:
Path to an absolute path of a font file to use for rendering
the text. See https://freetype.org/freetype2/docs/index.html for a list of
supported font file formats.

or ``annot=((lh_labels, lh_ctab), (rh_labels, rh_ctab))`` for both

by :func:`nibabel.freesurfer.io.read_annot`.

borders.description:
Show only label borders. If int, specify the number of steps
(away from the true border) along the cortical mesh to include
as part of the border definition.

hemi.description:
If None, it is assumed to belong to the hemisphere being
shown. If two hemispheres are being shown, data must exist
for both hemispheres.

row.description: The row to use, default is the first one.

col.description: The column to check, the default is the first one.

align.description:
If True, consider view arguments relative to canonical MRI
directions (closest to MNI for the subject) rather than native MRI
space. This helps when MRIs are not in standard orientation (e.g.,
have large rotations).

take precedence and modify the camera starting from the ``view``.

string shortcut options.

roll.description: The roll of the camera rendering the view in degrees.

distance.description:

used to set a reasonable distance.

directions (closest to MNI for the subject) rather than native MRI
space. This helps when MRIs are not in standard orientation (e.g.,
have large rotations).

The focal point of the camera rendering the view: (x, y, z) in
plot units (either m or mm). When ``"auto"``, it is set to the center of
mass of the visible bounds.

Force an update of the plot. Defaults to True.
