verbose.description:
Control verbosity of the logging output. If ``None``, use the default
verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

mode.description: Either ``'rgb'`` or ``'rgba'`` for values to return.

Brain.save_image.description: Save view from all panels to disk.

mode.description: Either ``'rgb'`` or ``'rgba'`` for values to return.

time_viewer.description:
If True, include time viewer traces. Only used if
``time_viewer=True`` and ``separate_canvas=False``.

Brain.screenshot.description: Generate a screenshot of current view.

fmin.description: Minimum value in colormap (uses real fmin if None).

fmid.description:
Intermediate value in colormap (fmid between fmin and
fmax if None).

fmax.description: Maximum value in colormap (uses real max if None).

Brain.update_lut.description: Update the range of the color map.

Brain.set_data_smoothing.description: Set the number of smoothing steps.

interpolation.description:
Interpolation method (:class:`scipy.interpolate.interp1d` parameter).
Must be one of ``'linear'``, ``'nearest'``, ``'zero'``, ``'slinear'``,
``'quadratic'`` or ``'cubic'``.

time_idx.description:
The time index to use. Can be a float to use interpolation
between indices.

Brain.set_time_point.description: Set the time point to display (can be a float to interpolate).

time.description: The time to show, in seconds.

Brain.set_time.description: Set the time to display (in seconds).

filename.description:
Path at which to save the movie. The extension determines the
format (e.g., ``'*.mov'``, ``'*.gif'``, ...; see the :mod:`imageio`
documentation for available formats).

time_dilation.description:
Factor by which to stretch time (default 4). For example, an epoch
from -100 to 600 ms lasts 700 ms. With ``time_dilation=4`` this
would result in a 2.8 s long movie.

tmin.description: First time point to include (default: all data).

tmax.description: Last time point to include (default: all data).

framerate.description: Framerate of the movie (frames per second, default 24).

interpolation.description:
Interpolation method (:class:`scipy.interpolate.interp1d` parameter).
Must be one of ``'linear'``, ``'nearest'``, ``'zero'``, ``'slinear'``,
``'quadratic'`` or ``'cubic'``.
If None, it uses the current ``brain.interpolation``,
which defaults to ``'nearest'``. Defaults to None.

callback.description:
A function to call on each iteration. Useful for status message
updates. It will be passed keyword arguments ``frame`` and
``n_frames``.

time_viewer.description:
If True, include time viewer traces. Only used if
``time_viewer=True`` and ``separate_canvas=False``.

Brain.save_movie.description:
The movie is created through the :mod:`imageio` module. The format is
determined by the extension, and additional options can be specified
through keyword arguments that depend on the format, see
:doc:`imageio's format page <imageio:formats/index>`.

.. Warning::
    This method assumes that time is specified in seconds when adding
    data. If time is specified in milliseconds this will result in
    movies 1000 times longer than expected.

Brain.get_picked_points.description: Return the vertices of the picked points.

imdata.description: The image that you wish to click on for 2-d points.

ClickableImage.description:
Takes as input an image array (can be any array that works with imshow,
but will work best with images.  Displays the image and lets you
click on it.  Stores the xy coordinates of each click, so now you can
superimpose something on top of it.

Upon clicking, the x/y coordinate of the cursor will be stored in
self.coords, which is a list of (x, y) tuples.

ClickableImage.plot_clicks.description: Plot the x/y positions stored in self.coords.

ClickableImage.to_layout.description: Normalizes by the image you used to generate clicks

surf_maps.description: The surface mapping information obtained with make_field_map.

time.description:
The time point at which the field map shall be displayed. If None,
the average peak latency (across sensor types) is used.

time_label.description: How to print info about the time instant visualized.

n_jobs.description:
The number of jobs to run in parallel. If ``-1``, it is set
to the number of CPU cores. Requires the :mod:`joblib` package.
``None`` (default) is a marker for 'unset' that will be interpreted
as ``n_jobs=1`` (sequential execution) unless the call is performed under
a :class:`joblib:joblib.parallel_config` context manager that sets another
value for ``n_jobs``.

vmax.description:
Maximum intensity. Can be a dictionary with two entries ``"eeg"`` and ``"meg"``
to specify separate values for EEG and MEG fields respectively. Can be
``None`` to use the maximum value of the data.

.. versionadded:: 0.21
.. versionadded:: 1.4
    ``vmax`` can be a dictionary to specify separate values for EEG and
    MEG fields.

show_density.description:
Whether to draw the field density as an overlay on top of the helmet/head
surface. Defaults to ``True``.

alpha.description:
Opacity of the meshes (between 0 and 1). Can be a dictionary with two
entries ``"eeg"`` and ``"meg"`` to specify separate values for EEG and
MEG fields respectively. Can be ``None`` to use 1.0 when a single field
map is shown, or ``dict(eeg=1.0, meg=0.5)`` when both field maps are shown.

.. versionadded:: 1.4

interpolation.description:
Interpolation method (:class:`scipy.interpolate.interp1d` parameter).
Must be one of ``'linear'``, ``'nearest'``, ``'zero'``, ``'slinear'``,
``'quadratic'`` or ``'cubic'``.

.. versionadded:: 1.6

interaction.description:
How interactions with the scene via an input device (e.g., mouse or
trackpad) modify the camera position. If ``'terrain'``, one axis is
fixed, enabling "turntable-style" rotations. If ``'trackball'``,
movement along all axes is possible, which provides more freedom of
movement, but you may incidentally perform unintentional rotations along
some axes.
Defaults to ``'terrain'``.

.. versionadded:: 1.1

time_viewer.description:
Display time viewer GUI. Can also be ``"auto"``, which will mean
``True`` if there is more than one time point and ``False`` otherwise.

.. versionadded:: 1.6

verbose.description:
Control verbosity of the logging output. If ``None``, use the default
verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

EvokedField.description: Plot MEG/EEG fields on head surface and helmet in 3D.

time.description: The time to show, in seconds.

EvokedField.set_time.description: Set the time to display (in seconds).

n_contours.description: The number of contour lines to use.

EvokedField.set_contours.description: Adjust the number of contour lines to use when drawing the fieldlines.

vmax.description: The new maximum value of the color range.

kind.description: Which field map to apply the new color range to.

EvokedField.set_vmax.description: Change the color range of the density maps.

im.description:
A background image for the figure. This must be a valid input to
`matplotlib.pyplot.imshow`. Defaults to None.

set_ratios.description:
Set the aspect ratio of any axes in fig
to the value in set_ratios. Defaults to None,
which does nothing to axes.

add_background_image.description:
Adds the image specified in ``im`` to the
figure ``fig``. This is generally meant to
be done with topo plots, though it could work
for any plot.

.. note:: This modifies the figure and/or axes in place.

fname_out.description:
Filename to store the resulting diff. If None, a temporary
file will be created.

show.description: If True, show the resulting diff in a new tab in a web browser.

read_limit.description:
Max number of bytes of data to read from a tag. Can be np.inf
to always read all data (helps test read completion).

max_str.description:
Max number of characters of string representation to print for
each tag's data.

verbose.description:
Control verbosity of the logging output. If ``None``, use the default
verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

compare_fiff.description: Compare the contents of two fiff files using diff and show_fiff.

node_order.description:
List with node names defining the order in which the nodes are
arranged. Must have the elements as node_names but the order can be
different. The nodes are arranged clockwise starting at "start_pos"
degrees.

start_pos.description: Angle in degrees that defines where the first node is plotted.

start_between.description:
If True, the layout starts with the position between the nodes. This is
the same as adding "180. / len(node_names)" to start_pos.

group_boundaries.description:
List of of boundaries between groups at which point a "group_sep" will
be inserted. E.g. "[0, len(node_names) / 2]" will create two groups.

group_sep.description: Group separation angle in degrees. See "group_boundaries".

circular_layout.description: Create layout arranging nodes on a circle.

on_pick.description:
The callback function to be invoked on clicking one
of the axes. Is supposed to instantiate the following
API: ``function(axis, channel_index)``.

fig_facecolor.description: The figure face color. Defaults to black.

axis_facecolor.description: The axis face color. Defaults to black.

axis_spinecolor.description:
The axis spine color. Defaults to black. In other words,
the color of the axis' edge lines.

layout_scale.description:
Scaling factor for adjusting the relative size of the layout
on the canvas. If None, nothing will be scaled.

legend.description:
If True, an additional axis is created in the bottom right corner
that can be used to, e.g., construct a legend. The index of this
axis will be -1.

select.description:
Whether to enable the lasso-selection tool to enable the user to select
channels. The selected channels will be available in
``fig.lasso.selection``.

.. versionadded:: 1.10.0

iter_topography.description:
This function returns a generator that unpacks into
a series of matplotlib axis objects and data / channel
indices, both corresponding to the sensor positions
of the related layout passed or inferred from the channel info.
Hence, this enables convenient topography plot customization.

format.description:
Type of colormap to return. If 'matplotlib', will return a
matplotlib.colors.LinearSegmentedColormap. If 'vtk', will
return an RGBA array of shape (256, 4).

mne_analyze_colormap.description: Return a colormap similar to that used by mne_analyze.

subject.description: The FreeSurfer subject name.

subjects_dir.description:
The path to the directory containing the FreeSurfer subjects
reconstructions. If ``None``, defaults to the ``SUBJECTS_DIR`` environment
variable.

slices.description:
The indices of the MRI slices to plot. If ``None``, automatically
pick 12 equally-spaced slices.

brain_surfaces.description:
One or more brain surface to plot (optional). Entries should correspond
to files in the subject's ``surf`` directory (e.g. ``"white"``).

show_indices.description:
Show slice indices if True.

.. versionadded:: 0.20

mri.description:
The name of the MRI to use. Can be a standard FreeSurfer MRI such as
``'T1.mgz'``, or a full path to a custom MRI file.

.. versionadded:: 0.21

show_orientation.description:
Show the orientation (L/R, P/A, I/S) of the data slices.
True (default) will only show it on the outside most edges of the
figure, False will never show labels, and "always" will label each
plot.

.. versionadded:: 0.21
.. versionchanged:: 0.24
   Added support for "always".

plot_bem.description: Plot BEM contours on anatomical MRI slices.

clim.description:
Colorbar properties specification. If 'auto', set clim automatically
based on data percentiles. If dict, should contain:

    ``kind`` : 'value' | 'percent'
        Flag to specify type of limits.
    ``lims`` : list | np.ndarray | tuple of float, 3 elements
        Lower, middle, and upper bounds for colormap.
    ``pos_lims`` : list | np.ndarray | tuple of float, 3 elements
        Lower, middle, and upper bound for colormap. Positive values
        will be mirrored directly across zero during colormap
        construction to obtain negative control points.

.. note:: Only one of ``lims`` or ``pos_lims`` should be provided.
          Only sequential colormaps should be used with ``lims``, and
          only divergent colormaps should be used with ``pos_lims``.

transparent.description:
If True: use a linear transparency between fmin and fmid
and make values below fmin fully transparent (symmetrically for
divergent colormaps). None will choose automatically based on colormap
type.

orientation.description: Orientation of the colorbar, can be "vertical" or "horizontal".

bgcolor.description: The color behind the colorbar (for alpha blending).

plot_brain_colorbar.description: Plot a colorbar that corresponds to a brain activation map.

bridged_idx.description:
The indices of channels marked as bridged with each bridged
pair stored as a tuple.
Can be generated via
:func:`mne.preprocessing.compute_bridged_electrodes`.

ed_matrix.description:
The electrical distance matrix for each pair of EEG electrodes.
Can be generated via
:func:`mne.preprocessing.compute_bridged_electrodes`.

title.description: A title to add to the plot.

plot_bridged_electrodes.description: Topoplot electrode distance matrix with bridged electrodes connected.

snr_dict.description:
The dictionary returned by `~mne.chpi.compute_chpi_snr`. Must have keys
``times``, ``freqs``, ``TYPE_snr``, ``TYPE_power``, and ``TYPE_resid``
(where ``TYPE`` can be ``mag`` or ``grad`` or both).

plot_chpi_snr.description: Plot time-varying SNR estimates of the HPI coils.

exclude.description:
List of channels to exclude. If empty do not exclude any channel.
If 'bads', exclude info['bads'].

colorbar.description: Show colorbar or not.

proj.description: Apply projections or not.

show_svd.description:
Plot also singular values of the noise covariance for each sensor
type. We show square roots ie. standard deviations.

verbose.description:
Control verbosity of the logging output. If ``None``, use the default
verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

labels.description: Lists of labels (values) associated with each channel (keys).

picks.description: The channels to consider.

plot_channel_labels_circle.description:
.. note:: This primarily makes sense for sEEG channels where each
          channel can be assigned an anatomical label as the electrode
          passes through various brain areas.

adjacency.description:
Array of channels x channels shape. Defines which channels are adjacent
to each other. Note that if you edit adjacencies
(via ``edit=True``), this array will be modified in place.

ch_names.description: Names of successive channels in the ``adjacency`` matrix.

kind.description: How to plot the adjacency. Can be either ``'3d'`` or ``'2d'``.

edit.description:
Whether to allow interactive editing of the adjacency matrix via
clicking respective channel pairs. Once clicked, the channel is
"activated" and turns green. Clicking on another channel adds or
removes adjacency relation between the activated and newly clicked
channel (depending on whether the channels are already adjacent or
not); the newly clicked channel now becomes activated. Clicking on
an activated channel deactivates it. Editing is currently only
supported for ``kind='2d'``.

mode.description:
Whether to plot the cross-spectral density ('csd', the default), or
the coherence ('coh') between the channels.

colorbar.description: Whether to show a colorbar. Defaults to ``True``.

cmap.description:
The matplotlib colormap to use. Defaults to None, which means the
colormap will default to matplotlib's default.

n_cols.description:
CSD matrices are plotted in a grid. This parameter controls how
many matrix to plot side by side before starting a new row. By
default, a number will be chosen to make the grid as square as
possible.

show.description: Whether to show the figure. Defaults to ``True``.

plot_csd.description:
A sub-plot is created for each frequency. If an info object is passed to
the function, different channel types are plotted in different figures.

colors.description: Color to plot with each dipole. If None default colors are used.

plot_dipole_amplitudes.description: Plot the amplitude traces of a set of dipoles.

trans.description:
The mri to head trans.
Can be None with mode set to '3d'.

subject.description:
The FreeSurfer subject name (will be used to set the FreeSurfer
environment variable ``SUBJECT``).
Can be ``None`` with mode set to ``'3d'``.

subjects_dir.description:
The path to the directory containing the FreeSurfer subjects
reconstructions. If ``None``, defaults to the ``SUBJECTS_DIR`` environment
variable.

mode.description:
Can be:

``'arrow'`` or ``'sphere'``
    Plot in 3D mode using PyVista with the given glyph type.
``'orthoview'``
    Plot in matplotlib ``Axes3D`` using matplotlib with MRI slices
    shown on the sides of a cube, with the dipole(s) shown as arrows
    extending outward from a dot (i.e., the arrows pivot on the tail).
``'outlines'``
    Plot in matplotlib ``Axes`` using a quiver of arrows for the
    dipoles in three axes (axial, coronal, and sagittal views),
    with the arrow pivoting in the middle of the arrow.

.. versionchanged:: 1.1
   Added support for ``'outlines'``.

coord_frame.description:
Coordinate frame to use: 'head' or 'mri'. Can also be 'mri_rotated'
when mode equals ``'outlines'``. Defaults to 'mri'.

.. versionadded:: 0.14.0
.. versionchanged:: 1.1
   Added support for ``'mri_rotated'``.

idx.description:
Index of the initially plotted dipole. Can also be 'gof' to plot the
dipole with highest goodness of fit value or 'amplitude' to plot the
dipole with the highest amplitude. The dipoles can also be browsed
through using up/down arrow keys or mouse scroll. Defaults to 'gof'.
Only used if mode equals 'orthoview'.

.. versionadded:: 0.14.0

show_all.description:
Whether to always plot all the dipoles. If ``True`` (default), the
active dipole is plotted as a red dot and its location determines the
shown MRI slices. The non-active dipoles are plotted as small blue
dots. If ``False``, only the active dipole is plotted.
Only used if ``mode='orthoview'``.

.. versionadded:: 0.14.0

block.description:
Whether to halt program execution until the figure is closed. Defaults
to False.
Only used if mode equals 'orthoview'.

.. versionadded:: 0.14.0

show.description:
Show figure if True. Defaults to True.
Only used if mode equals 'orthoview'.

scale.description:
The scale (size in meters) of the dipoles if ``mode`` is not
``'orthoview'``. The default is 0.03 when mode is ``'outlines'`` and
0.005 otherwise.

color.description:
The color of the dipoles.
The default (None) will use ``'y'`` if mode is ``'orthoview'`` and
``show_all`` is True, else 'r'. Can also be a list of colors to use
when mode is ``'outlines'``.

.. versionchanged:: 0.19.0
   Color is now passed in orthoview mode.

highlight_color.description:
The highlight color. Only used in orthoview mode with
``show_all=True``.

.. versionadded:: 0.19.0

title.description:
The title of the figure if ``mode='orthoview'`` (ignored for all other
modes). If ``None``, dipole number and its properties (amplitude,
orientation etc.) will be shown. Defaults to ``None``.

.. versionadded:: 0.21.0

head_source.description:
Head source(s) to use. See the ``source`` option of
:func:`mne.get_head_surf` for more information.
Only used when mode equals ``'outlines'``.

.. versionadded:: 1.1

surf.description:
Brain surface to show outlines for, can be ``'white'``, ``'pial'``, or
``None``. Only used when mode is ``'outlines'``.

.. versionadded:: 1.1

width.description:
Width of the matplotlib quiver arrow, see
:meth:`matplotlib:matplotlib.axes.Axes.quiver`. If None (default),
when mode is ``'outlines'`` 0.015 will be used, and when mode is
``'orthoview'`` the matplotlib default is used.

verbose.description:
Control verbosity of the logging output. If ``None``, use the default
verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

plot_dipole_locations.description:
If mode is set to 'arrow' or 'sphere', only the location of the first
time point of each dipole is shown else use the show_all parameter.

threshold.description:
The percentage threshold to use to decide whether or not to
plot. Default is zero (always plot).

n_max_plot.description: Maximum number of channels to show stats for.

subject.description:
The subject name to use in the title of the plot. If ``None``, do not
display a subject name.

.. versionchanged:: 0.23
   Added support for ``None``.

.. versionchanged:: 1.0
   Defaults to ``None``.

color.description: Color to use for the bars.

plot_drop_log.description: Show the channel stats based on a drop_log from Epochs.

picks.description:
Channels to include. Slices and lists of integers will be interpreted as 
channel indices. In lists, channel *type* strings (e.g., ``['meg', 
'eeg']``) will pick channels of those types, channel *name* strings (e.g., 
``['MEG0111', 'MEG2623']`` will pick the given channels. Can also be the 
string values ``'all'`` to pick all channels, or ``'data'`` to pick 
:term:`data channels`. None (default) will pick good data channels. Note 
that channels in ``info['bads']`` *will be included* if their names or 
indices are explicitly provided.

scalings.description:
Scaling factors for the traces. If a dictionary where any
value is ``'auto'``, the scaling factor is set to match the 99.5th
percentile of the respective data. If ``'auto'``, all scalings (for all
channel types) are set to ``'auto'``. If any values are ``'auto'`` and the
data is not preloaded, a subset up to 100 MB will be loaded. If ``None``,
defaults to::

    dict(mag=1e-12, grad=4e-11, eeg=20e-6, eog=150e-6, ecg=5e-4,
         emg=1e-3, ref_meg=1e-12, misc=1e-3, stim=1,
         resp=1, chpi=1e-4, whitened=1e2)

.. note::
    A particular scaling value ``s`` corresponds to half of the visualized
    signal range around zero (i.e. from ``0`` to ``+s`` or from ``0`` to
    ``-s``). For example, the default scaling of ``20e-6`` (20µV) for EEG
    signals means that the visualized range will be 40 µV (20 µV in the
    positive direction and 20 µV in the negative direction).

n_epochs.description: The number of epochs per view. Defaults to 20.

n_channels.description: The number of channels per view. Defaults to 20.

title.description:
The title of the window. If None, the event names (from
``epochs.event_id``) will be displayed. Defaults to None.

event_color.description:
Color(s) to use for :term:`events`. To show all :term:`events` in the same
color, pass any matplotlib-compatible color. To color events differently,
pass a `dict` that maps event names or integer event numbers to colors
(must include entries for *all* events, or include a "fallback" entry with
key ``-1``). If ``None``, colors are chosen from the current Matplotlib
color cycle.
Defaults to ``None``.

order.description:
Order in which to plot data. If the array is shorter than the number of
channels, only the given channels are plotted. If ``None`` (default), all
channels are plotted. If ``group_by`` is ``'position'`` or
``'selection'``, the ``order`` parameter is used only for selecting the
channels to be plotted.

.. versionadded:: 0.18.0

show.description: Show figure if True. Defaults to True.

block.description:
Whether to halt program execution until the figure is closed.
Useful for rejecting bad trials on the fly by clicking on an epoch.
Defaults to False.

decim.description:
Amount to decimate the data during display for speed purposes.
You should only decimate if the data are sufficiently low-passed,
otherwise aliasing can occur. The 'auto' mode (default) uses
the decimation that results in a sampling rate at least three times
larger than ``info['lowpass']`` (e.g., a 40 Hz lowpass will result in
at least a 120 Hz displayed sample rate).

.. versionadded:: 0.15.0

butterfly.description:
Whether to directly call the butterfly view.

.. versionadded:: 0.18.0

show_scrollbars.description:
Whether to show scrollbars when the plot is initialized. Can be toggled
after initialization by pressing :kbd:`z` ("zen mode") while the plot
window is focused. Default is ``True``.

.. versionadded:: 0.19.0

show_scalebars.description:
Whether to show scale bars when the plot is initialized. Can be toggled
after initialization by pressing :kbd:`s` while the plot window is focused.
Default is ``True``.

.. versionadded:: 0.24.0

group_by.description:
How to group channels. ``'type'`` groups by channel type,
``'original'`` plots in the order of ch_names, ``'selection'`` uses
Elekta's channel groupings (only works for Neuromag data),
``'position'`` groups the channels by the positions of the sensors.
``'selection'`` and ``'position'`` modes allow custom selections by
using a lasso selector on the topomap. In butterfly mode, ``'type'``
and ``'original'`` group the channels by type, whereas ``'selection'``
and ``'position'`` use regional grouping. ``'type'`` and ``'original'``
modes are ignored when ``order`` is not ``None``. Defaults to ``'type'``.

precompute.description:
Whether to load all data (not just the visible portion) into RAM and
apply preprocessing (e.g., projectors) to the full data array in a separate
processor thread, instead of window-by-window during scrolling. The default
None uses the ``MNE_BROWSER_PRECOMPUTE`` variable, which defaults to
``'auto'``. ``'auto'`` compares available RAM space to the expected size of
the precomputed data, and precomputes only if enough RAM is available.
This is only used with the Qt backend.

.. versionadded:: 0.24
.. versionchanged:: 1.0
   Support for the ``MNE_BROWSER_PRECOMPUTE`` config variable.

use_opengl.description:
Whether to use OpenGL when rendering the plot (requires ``pyopengl``).
May increase performance, but effect is dependent on system CPU and
graphics hardware. Only works if using the Qt backend. Default is
None, which will use False unless the user configuration variable
``MNE_BROWSER_USE_OPENGL`` is set to ``'true'``,
see :func:`mne.set_config`.

.. versionadded:: 0.24

theme.description:
Can be "auto", "light", or "dark" or a path-like to a
custom stylesheet. For Dark-Mode and automatic Dark-Mode-Detection,
`qdarkstyle <https://github.com/ColinDuquesnoy/QDarkStyleSheet>`__ and
`darkdetect <https://github.com/albertosottile/darkdetect>`__,
respectively, are required.    If None (default), the config option MNE_BROWSER_THEME will be used,
defaulting to "auto" if it's not found.
For the ``"matplotlib"`` backend, only ``"light"``, ``"dark"``,
and ``"auto"`` are supported. For the ``"qt"`` backend, a path-like to a custom
stylesheet is also accepted.

.. versionadded:: 1.0

overview_mode.description:
Can be "channels", "empty", or "hidden" to set the overview bar mode
for the ``'qt'`` backend. If None (default), the config option
``MNE_BROWSER_OVERVIEW_MODE`` will be used, defaulting to "channels"
if it's not found.

.. versionadded:: 1.1

splash.description:
If True (default), a splash screen is shown during the application startup. Only
applicable to the ``qt`` backend.

.. versionadded:: 1.6

annotation_colors.description:
A dictionary mapping annotation description strings to colors. Use this to
override the default color assigned to specific annotation types (e.g.,
``dict(bad_segment='orange')``). Colors can be any valid Matplotlib color
specification. Keys that do not match any annotation description in the data
will trigger a warning. If ``None`` (default), automatic colors are used.

.. versionadded:: 1.12.1

plot_epochs.description:
Bad epochs can be marked with a left click on top of the epoch. Bad
channels can be selected by clicking the channel name on the left side of
the main axes. Calling this function drops all the selected bad epochs as
well as bad epochs marked beforehand with rejection parameters.

bands.description:
The frequencies or frequency ranges to plot. If a :class:`dict`, keys will
be used as subplot titles and values should be either a single frequency
(e.g., ``{'presentation rate': 6.5}``) or a length-two sequence of lower
and upper frequency band edges (e.g., ``{'theta': (4, 8)}``). If a single
frequency is provided, the plot will show the frequency bin that is closest
to the requested value. If ``None`` (the default), expands to::

    bands = {'Delta (0-4 Hz)': (0, 4), 'Theta (4-8 Hz)': (4, 8),
             'Alpha (8-12 Hz)': (8, 12), 'Beta (12-30 Hz)': (12, 30),
             'Gamma (30-45 Hz)': (30, 45)}

.. note::
   For backwards compatibility, :class:`tuples<tuple>` of length 2 or 3 are
   also accepted, where the last element of the tuple is the subplot title
   and the other entries are frequency values (a single value or band
   edges). New code should use :class:`dict` or ``None``.

.. versionchanged:: 1.2
   Allow passing a dict and discourage passing tuples.

tmin.description:
First and last times to include, in seconds. ``None`` uses the first or
last time present in the data. Default is ``tmin=None, tmax=None`` (all
times).

tmax.description:
First and last times to include, in seconds. ``None`` uses the first or
last time present in the data. Default is ``tmin=None, tmax=None`` (all
times).

proj.description:
Whether to apply SSP projection vectors before spectral estimation.
Default is ``False``.

bandwidth.description:
The bandwidth of the multi taper windowing function in Hz. The default
value is a window half-bandwidth of 4 Hz.

adaptive.description:
Use adaptive weights to combine the tapered spectra into PSD
(slow, use n_jobs >> 1 to speed up computation).

low_bias.description:
Only use tapers with more than 90% spectral concentration within
bandwidth.

normalization.description:
Normalization strategy. If "full", the PSD will be normalized by the
sampling rate as well as the length of the signal (as in
:ref:`Nitime <nitime:users-guide>`). Default is ``'length'``.

ch_type.description:
The channel type to plot. For ``'grad'``, the gradiometers are
collected in pairs and the mean for each pair is plotted. If
``None`` the first available channel type from order shown above is used. Defaults to ``None``.

normalize.description:
If True, each band will be divided by the total power. Defaults to
False.

agg_fun.description:
The function used to aggregate over frequencies. Defaults to
:func:`numpy.sum` if ``normalize=True``, else :func:`numpy.mean`.

dB.description:
Whether to plot on a decibel scale. If ``True``, plots
10 × log₁₀(spectral_power/Hz), following the application of ``agg_fun``. Ignored if ``normalize=True``.

sensors.description:
Whether to add markers for sensor locations. If :class:`str`, should be a
valid matplotlib format string (e.g., ``'r+'`` for red plusses, see the
Notes section of :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.plot`). If ``True`` (the
default), black circles will be used.

names.description:
Labels for the sensors. If a :class:`list`, labels should correspond
to the order of channels in ``data``. If ``None`` (default), no channel
names are plotted.

mask.description:
Array indicating channel-time combinations to highlight with a distinct
plotting style (useful for, e.g. marking which channels at which times a statistical test of the data reaches significance). Array elements set to ``True`` will be plotted
with the parameters given in ``mask_params``. Defaults to ``None``,
equivalent to an array of all ``False`` elements.

mask_params.description:
Additional plotting parameters for plotting significant sensors.
Default (None) equals::

    dict(marker='o', markerfacecolor='w', markeredgecolor='k',
            linewidth=0, markersize=4)

contours.description:
The number of contour lines to draw. If ``0``, no contours will be drawn.
If a positive integer, that number of contour levels are chosen using the
matplotlib tick locator (may sometimes be inaccurate, use array for
accuracy). If array-like, the array values are used as the contour levels.
The values should be in µV for EEG, fT for magnetometers and fT/m for
gradiometers. If ``colorbar=True``, the colorbar will have ticks
corresponding to the contour levels. Default is ``6``.

outlines.description:
The outlines to be drawn. If 'head', the default head scheme will be
drawn. If dict, each key refers to a tuple of x and y positions, the values
in 'mask_pos' will serve as image mask.
Alternatively, a matplotlib patch object can be passed for advanced
masking options, either directly or as a function that returns patches
(required for multi-axis plots). If None, nothing will be drawn.
Defaults to 'head'.

image_interp.description:
The image interpolation to be used. Options are ``'cubic'`` (default)
to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.CloughTocher2DInterpolator`,
``'nearest'`` to use :class:`scipy.spatial.Voronoi` or
``'linear'`` to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.LinearNDInterpolator`.

extrapolate.description:
Options:

- ``'box'``
    Extrapolate to four points placed to form a square encompassing all
    data points, where each side of the square is three times the range
    of the data in the respective dimension.
- ``'local'`` (default for MEG sensors)
    Extrapolate only to nearby points (approximately to points closer than
    median inter-electrode distance). This will also set the
    mask to be polygonal based on the convex hull of the sensors.
- ``'head'`` (default for non-MEG sensors)
    Extrapolate out to the edges of the clipping circle. This will be on
    the head circle when the sensors are contained within the head circle,
    but it can extend beyond the head when sensors are plotted outside
    the head circle.

.. versionchanged:: 0.21

   - The default was changed to ``'local'`` for MEG sensors.
   - ``'local'`` was changed to use a convex hull mask
   - ``'head'`` was changed to extrapolate out to the clipping circle.

border.description:
Value to extrapolate to on the topomap borders. If ``'mean'`` (default),
then each extrapolated point has the average value of its neighbours.

.. versionadded:: 0.20

res.description: The resolution of the topomap image (number of pixels along each side).

size.description: Side length of each subplot in inches.

vlim.description:
Lower and upper bounds of the colormap, typically a numeric value in the same
units as the data. Elements of the :class:`tuple` may also be callable functions
which take in a :class:`NumPy array <numpy.ndarray>` and return a scalar.

If both entries are ``None``, the bounds are set at ± the maximum absolute value
of the data (yielding a colormap with midpoint at 0), or ``(0, max(abs(data)))``
if the (possibly baselined) data are all-positive.
Providing ``None`` for just one entry will set the corresponding boundary at the
min/max of the data. If ``vlim="joint"``, will compute the colormap limits
jointly across all topomaps of the same channel type (instead of separately
for each topomap), using the min/max of the data for that channel type.
Defaults to ``(None, None)``.

.. versionadded:: 0.21

colorbar.description: Plot a colorbar in the rightmost column of the figure.

cbar_fmt.description:
Formatting string for colorbar tick labels. See :ref:`formatspec` for
details.
If ``'auto'``, is equivalent to '%0.3f' if ``dB=False`` and '%0.1f' if
``dB=True``. Defaults to ``'auto'``.

units.description:
The units to use for the colorbar label. Ignored if ``colorbar=False``.
If ``None`` the label will be "AU" indicating arbitrary units.
Default is ``None``.

n_jobs.description:
The number of jobs to run in parallel. If ``-1``, it is set
to the number of CPU cores. Requires the :mod:`joblib` package.
``None`` (default) is a marker for 'unset' that will be interpreted
as ``n_jobs=1`` (sequential execution) unless the call is performed under
a :class:`joblib:joblib.parallel_config` context manager that sets another
value for ``n_jobs``.

verbose.description:
Control verbosity of the logging output. If ``None``, use the default
verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

plot_epochs_psd_topomap.description: Plot the topomap of the power spectral density across epochs.

sfreq.description:
The sample frequency. If None, data will be displayed in samples (not
seconds).

first_samp.description:
The index of the first sample. Recordings made on Neuromag systems
number samples relative to the system start (not relative to the
beginning of the recording). In such cases the ``raw.first_samp``
attribute can be passed here. Default is 0.

color.description:
Dictionary of event_id integers as keys and colors as values. If None,
colors are automatically drawn from a default list (cycled through if
number of events longer than list of default colors). Color can be any
valid :ref:`matplotlib color <matplotlib:colors_def>`.

equal_spacing.description: Use equal spacing between events in y-axis.

on_missing.description:
Can be ``'raise'`` (default) to raise an error, ``'warn'`` to emit a
warning, or ``'ignore'`` to ignore when event numbers from ``event_id`` are missing from
:term:`events`. When numbers from :term:`events` are missing from
``event_id`` they will be ignored and a warning emitted; consider
using ``verbose='error'`` in this case.

.. versionadded:: 0.21

verbose.description:
Control verbosity of the logging output. If ``None``, use the default
verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

plot_events.description: Plot :term:`events` to get a visual display of the paradigm.

picks.description:
Channels to include. Slices and lists of integers will be interpreted as 
channel indices. In lists, channel *type* strings (e.g., ``['meg', 
'eeg']``) will pick channels of those types, channel *name* strings (e.g., 
``['MEG0111', 'MEG2623']`` will pick the given channels. Can also be the 
string values ``'all'`` to pick all channels, or ``'data'`` to pick 
:term:`data channels`. None (default) will pick all channels. Bad channels 
are included by default. Note that channels in ``info['bads']`` *will be 
included* if their names or indices are explicitly provided.

exclude.description:
Channels names to exclude from being shown. If ``'bads'``, the
bad channels are excluded.

ylim.description:
Y-axis limits for plots (after scaling has been applied). :class:`dict`
keys should match channel types; valid keys are for instance ``eeg``, ``mag``,
``grad``, ``misc``, ``csd``, .. (example: ``ylim=dict(eeg=[-20, 20])``). If
``None``, the y-axis limits will be set automatically by matplotlib. Defaults to
``None``.

xlim.description: Limits for the X-axis of the plots.

proj.description:
If true SSP projections are applied before display. If ``'interactive'``,
a check box for reversible selection of SSP projection vectors will
be shown. If ``'reconstruct'``, projection vectors will be applied and then
M/EEG data will be reconstructed via field mapping to reduce the signal
bias caused by projection.

.. versionchanged:: 0.21
   Support for 'reconstruct' was added.

hline.description: The values at which to show an horizontal line.

units.description:
The units of the channel types used for axes labels. If None,
defaults to ``dict(eeg='µV', grad='fT/cm', mag='fT')``.

scalings.description:
The scalings of the channel types to be applied for plotting. If None,
defaults to ``dict(eeg=1e6, grad=1e13, mag=1e15)``.

titles.description:
The titles associated with the channels. If None, defaults to
``dict(eeg='EEG', grad='Gradiometers', mag='Magnetometers')``.

gfp.description:
Plot the global field power (GFP) or the root mean square (RMS) of the
data. For MEG data, this will plot the RMS. For EEG, it plots GFP,
i.e. the standard deviation of the signal across channels. The GFP is
equivalent to the RMS of an average-referenced signal.

- ``True``
    Plot GFP or RMS (for EEG and MEG, respectively) and traces for all
    channels.
- ``'only'``
    Plot GFP or RMS (for EEG and MEG, respectively), and omit the
    traces for individual channels.

The color of the GFP/RMS trace will be green if
``spatial_colors=False``, and black otherwise.

.. versionchanged:: 0.23
   Plot GFP for EEG instead of RMS. Label RMS traces correctly as such.

window_title.description: The title to put at the top of the figure.

spatial_colors.description:
If True, the lines are color coded by mapping physical sensor
coordinates into color values. Spatially similar channels will have
similar colors. Bad channels will be dotted. If False, the good
channels are plotted black and bad channels red. If ``'auto'``, uses
True if channel locations are present, and False if channel locations
are missing or if the data contains only a single channel. Defaults to
``'auto'``.

zorder.description:
Which channels to put in the front or back. Only matters if
``spatial_colors`` is used.
If str, must be ``std`` or ``unsorted`` (defaults to ``unsorted``). If
``std``, data with the lowest standard deviation (weakest effects) will
be put in front so that they are not obscured by those with stronger
effects. If ``unsorted``, channels are z-sorted as in the evoked
instance.
If callable, must take one argument: a numpy array of the same
dimensionality as the evoked raw data; and return a list of
unique integers corresponding to the number of channels.

.. versionadded:: 0.13.0

selectable.description:
Whether to use interactive features. If True (default), it is possible
to paint an area to draw topomaps. When False, the interactive features
are disabled. Disabling interactive features reduces memory consumption
and is useful when using ``axes`` parameter to draw multiaxes figures.

.. versionadded:: 0.13.0

time_unit.description:
The units for the time axis, can be "s" (default) or "ms".

.. versionadded:: 0.16

highlight.description:
Segments of the data to highlight by means of a light-yellow
background color. Can be used to put visual emphasis on certain
time periods. The time periods must be specified as ``array-like``
objects in the form of ``(t_start, t_end)`` in the unit given by the
``time_unit`` parameter.
Multiple time periods can be specified by passing an ``array-like``
object of individual time periods (e.g., for 3 time periods, the shape
of the passed object would be ``(3, 2)``. If ``None``, no highlighting
is applied.

.. versionadded:: 1.1

verbose.description:
Control verbosity of the logging output. If ``None``, use the default
verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and
:func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword
argument.

plot_evoked.description:
Left click to a line shows the channel name. Selecting an area by clicking
and holding left mouse button plots a topographic map of the painted area.

.. note:: If bad channels are not excluded they are shown in red.

picks.description:
Channels to include. Slices and lists of integers will be interpreted as 
channel indices. In lists, channel *type* strings (e.g., ``['meg', 
'eeg']``) will pick channels of those types, channel *name* strings (e.g., 
``['MEG0111', 'MEG2623']`` will pick the given channels. Can also be the 
string values ``'all'`` to pick all channels, or ``'data'`` to pick 
:term:`data channels`. None (default) will pick all channels. Bad channels 
are included by default. Note that channels in ``info['bads']`` *will be 
included* if their names or indices are explicitly provided.
This parameter can also be used to set the order the channels
are shown in, as the channel image is sorted by the order of picks.

exclude.description:
Channels names to exclude from being shown. If 'bads', the
bad channels are excluded.

clim.description:
Color limits for plots (after scaling has been applied). e.g.
``clim = dict(eeg=[-20, 20])``.
Valid keys are eeg, mag, grad, misc. If None, the clim parameter
for each channel equals the pyplot default.

proj.description:
If true SSP projections are applied before display. If 'interactive',
a check box for reversible selection of SSP projection vectors will
be shown.

units.description:
The units of the channel types used for axes labels. If None,
defaults to ``dict(eeg='µV', grad='fT/cm', mag='fT')``.

scalings.description:
The scalings of the channel types to be applied for plotting. If None,`
defaults to ``dict(eeg=1e6, grad=1e13, mag=1e15)``.

titles.description:
The titles associated with the channels. If None, defaults to
``dict(eeg='EEG', grad='Gradiometers', mag='Magnetometers')``.

colorbar.description:
If True, plot a colorbar. Defaults to True.

.. versionadded:: 0.16

mask.description:
An array of booleans of the same shape as the data. Entries of the
data that correspond to ``False`` in the mask are masked (see
``do_mask`` below). Useful for, e.g., masking for statistical
significance.

.. versionadded:: 0.16

mask_style.description:
If ``mask`` is not None: if 'contour', a contour line is drawn around
the masked areas (``True`` in ``mask``). If 'mask', entries not
``True`` in ``mask`` are shown transparently. If 'both', both a contour
and transparency are used.
If ``None``, defaults to 'both' if ``mask`` is not None, and is ignored
otherwise.

 .. versionadded:: 0.16

mask_alpha.description:
A float between 0 and 1. If ``mask`` is not None, this sets the
alpha level (degree of transparency) for the masked-out segments.
I.e., if 0, masked-out segments are not visible at all.
Defaults to .25.

.. versionadded:: 0.16

time_unit.description:
The units for the time axis, can be "ms" or "s" (default).

.. versionadded:: 0.16

show_names.description:
Determines if channel names should be plotted on the y axis. If False,
no names are shown. If True, ticks are set automatically by matplotlib
and the corresponding channel names are shown. If "all", all channel
names are shown. If "auto", is set to False if ``picks`` is ``None``,
to ``True`` if ``picks`` contains 25 or more entries, or to "all"
if ``picks`` contains fewer than 25 entries.

group_by.description:
If a dict, the values must be picks, and ``axes`` must also be a dict
with matching keys, or None. If ``axes`` is None, one figure and one
axis will be created for each entry in ``group_by``.Then, for each
entry, the picked channels will be plotted to the corresponding axis.
If ``titles`` are None, keys will become plot titles. This is useful
for e.g. ROIs. Each entry must contain only one channel type.
For example::

    group_by=dict(Left_ROI=[1, 2, 3, 4], Right_ROI=[5, 6, 7, 8])

If None, all picked channels are plotted to the same axis.

layout_scale.description:
Scaling factor for adjusting the relative size of the layout
on the canvas.

color.description:
Everything matplotlib accepts to specify colors. If not list-like,
the color specified will be repeated. If None, colors are
automatically drawn.

border.description: Matplotlib borders style to be used for each sensor plot.

ylim.description:
Y-axis limits for plots (after scaling has been applied). :class:`dict`
keys should match channel types; valid keys are for instance ``eeg``, ``mag``,
``grad``, ``misc``, ``csd``, .. (example: ``ylim=dict(eeg=[-20, 20])``). If
``None``, the y-axis limits will be set automatically by matplotlib. Defaults to
``None``.

scalings.description:
The scalings of the channel types to be applied for plotting. If None,`
defaults to ``dict(eeg=1e6, grad=1e13, mag=1e15)``.

title.description: Title of the figure.

proj.description:
If true SSP projections are applied before display. If ``'interactive'``,
a check box for reversible selection of SSP projection vectors will
be shown.

vline.description: The values at which to show a vertical line.

fig_background.description:
A background image for the figure. This must work with a call to
``plt.imshow``. Defaults to None.

merge_grads.description:
Whether to use RMS value of gradiometer pairs. Only works for Neuromag
data. Defaults to False.

legend.description:
If True, create a legend based on evoked.comment. If False, disable the
legend. Otherwise, the legend is created and the parameter value is
passed as the location parameter to the matplotlib legend call. It can
be an integer (e.g. 0 corresponds to upper right corner of the plot),
a string (e.g. ``'upper right'``), or a tuple (x, y coordinates of the
lower left corner of the legend in the axes coordinate system).
See matplotlib documentation for more details.

background_color.description:
Background color. Typically ``'k'`` (black) or ``'w'`` (white; default).

.. versionadded:: 0.15.0

exclude.description:
Channels names to exclude from the plot. If ``'bads'``, the
bad channels are excluded. By default, exclude is set to ``'bads'``.

select.description:
Whether to enable the lasso-selection tool to enable the user to select
channels. The selected channels will be available in
``fig.lasso.selection``.

.. versionadded:: 1.10.0

plot_evoked_topo.description:
Clicking on the plot of an individual sensor opens a new figure showing
the evoked response for the selected sensor.

times.description:
The time point(s) to plot. If "auto", the number of ``axes`` determines

topographies will be shown with a regular time spacing between the
first and last time instant. If "peaks", finds time points
automatically by checking for local maxima in global field power. If
"interactive", the time can be set interactively at run-time by using a
slider.

average.description:
The time window (in seconds) around a given time point to be used for
averaging. For example, 0.2 would translate into a time window that
starts 0.1 s before and ends 0.1 s after the given time point. If the
time window exceeds the duration of the data, it will be clipped.
Different time windows (one per time point) can be provided by
passing an ``array-like`` object (e.g., ``[0.1, 0.2, 0.3]``). If
``None`` (default), no averaging will take place.

.. versionchanged:: 1.1
   Support for ``array-like`` input.
